exclusions.reason: Cover, publication date, contacts and association imprint only; no additional material substantive premise.

The €50/MWh all-in target and demands for a larger permanent grant are preferences. Future electrification demand, employment effects, unavoidable future tariff rises and the 20%/€50m steel-cost forecast are conditional predictions without a disclosed plant-level model; their accounting premises are separately checked.

Structural-reform demands, fiscal-affordability judgements, no expected competitive distortion, future investment/acceptance effects and preferred carbon-dividend design are evaluations or forecasts. The concrete amount, term, cascading, transparency and underlying-cost mechanism are inventoried.

Predicted investment deferral, competitiveness and climate-strategy harm, judgement that three years is insufficient certainty, and demands to transfer costs to the budget are normative or future outcomes. Legal policy promises and current tax scope are inventoried.
Contacts, 79 chambers, membership and overseas-network organisational description are low-priority background, not central cost or feasibility premises.

The €50/MWh target, adequacy of a €16.575bn grant against cumulative capital investment, stronger grant demands and preferred public cost sharing are evaluations. Predicted industry-aid interaction and future cost/investment harm are forecasts. General rising investment is checked through the dated 2024 figure; no universal annually increasing time series is inferred. Organisational history and member-share boilerplate are low-priority.
Title and author date only.

Retail association size, turnover and store counts are low-priority organisational description. Future actual net-tariff doubling is not tested as a realised fact; BNetzA and Frontier model attribution and assumptions are inventoried. Demands for permanent grants and interpretations of planning certainty are policy judgements.

Long investment cycles are contextual; predicted 2030 price jump and completed future AgNes process are forecasts, not observed outcomes. Recommended financing source and preferred grant amount are normative. Association membership boilerplate is incidental.

Preference for a general tax cut, comparative bureaucracy and transparency design, KTF opportunity-cost preferences, potential PPA attractiveness, competitiveness and future investment effects are proposals or conditional forecasts. The concrete current tax/duty/contract rules and their accounting mechanisms are separately inventoried; no future implementation cost is treated as measured. Member-interest and registration boilerplate are low-priority.

examples: Membership and group counts, brands and services; institutional contacts.

exclusions.reason: Preferences, fairness evaluations, rhetorical characterisations and unbounded future effects are not independently testable factual findings.
examples: Horizontal policy is fairer; selective relief is unjustified; general tax reduction preferred; long-term rule-based subsidy desired; fixed subsidy is inadequate for planning.

exclusions.reason: Future annual cost, per-kWh relief and investment outcomes are conditional forecasts; only their explicit arithmetic/structural premises are inventoried.
examples: Growing future cost base and decreasing future relief per kWh; future electrification attractiveness and economic viability.

exclusions.reason: Cover and organisational/contact/profile information has no additional material cost/benefit/legal premise.
examples: Author date, addresses, registry numbers and rounded membership/employment profile.

exclusions.reason: Preferences, business-value judgments and forecasts are excluded; factual duration, tax, mechanism and pass-through premises are retained.
examples: Competitive prices are important; subsidy is insufficient; structural reform needed; financing is politically fragile; possible burden jump after 2029.

exclusions.reason: Organisational profile and rhetorical prioritisation are low-priority context.
examples: Over 5000 members; electricity price is the central competitive lever.

exclusions.reason: Requested amounts and financing reforms are normative; future investment, transformation and price effects are forecasts.
examples: Keep €6.5bn; move levies into federal budget; strengthen competitiveness and avoid delaying electrification.

exclusions.reason: Policy requests and unquantified fears about future reforms are judgments/forecasts.
examples: Permanent competitive tariffs; closer regulator/government coordination; reform may shift costs against industry; delete §24d(6).

exclusions.reason: Organisational economic profile and contacts are low-priority descriptive background, not separate material policy premises.
examples: Staff/contact details, member count, sector turnover/employment.

exclusions.reason: Policy priorities and future harm/benefit forecasts are excluded while material numerical, legal and present-policy premises are retained.
examples: Public ownership preferred; energy poverty/deindustrialisation risks; electricity prices should be lower; stabilisation and further measures demanded.

exclusions.reason: References to DGB’s own previous advocacy are not independent external factual premises merely because footnoted.
examples: Previous positions on industrial price, StromVKG, EEG and grid reform; contact information.

exclusions.reason: Proposed stabilisation account design, desired targets, guardrails and future policy benefits are normative proposals.
examples: 2025 target corridor; minimum account funding, reserve and federal guarantee; public top-up, annual reports, ten-year planning horizon, voluntary flexibility.

exclusions.reason: Conditional technical examples are checked only as conditional arithmetic, not manufactured predictions; contacts and institutional statements are low-priority.
examples: 5%,10%,15% cost scenarios; exact future bills and investments; Good Work and transformation priorities.

exclusions.reason: Policy demands for equal household relief, tax/levy cuts and immediate enforcement are preferences. Assessments of inadequate or unfair relief are judgments; the numerical and legal premises are inventoried. Impressum, contacts and registration information are incidental.
The 2027 retail-price increase is a forecast. The attributed Verivox calculation and its assumptions are checked as a model description, not an observed future outcome.
Title, contents, authored date, member-market shares, registration and compliance boilerplate are low-priority organisational description.

Welcome, planning certainty, expected future jobs and benefits of modernisation are policy framing or forecasts. Faster legislation, predicted customer uncertainty and requests to remove information duties are preferences or predictions. Specific legal, timing and funding premises are inventoried.

The desirability of electrification, defossilisation, sovereignty and structural reform are policy judgments. Future prices not falling and predicted renewable-expansion effects are forecasts. Contacts are incidental.

Compatibility with future EU law is expressly a cautious interpretation and request for amendment, not a categorical ban claim. Requests for 2029 clarification and an annual reconciliation option are proposals. Actual draft premises are inventoried.

Calls for faster electrification, energy independence, a €6.5 billion subsidy and removal of fossil subsidies are preferences. Future investment responses and required political ambition are predictions or judgments. Conditional cost and flexibility mechanisms were checked separately.
Desired tax and levy reductions, the judgment that the cut is inappropriate and future planning benefits are preferences or forecasts. Contact and registration details are incidental.

The possibility that the cut fully offsets industrial-price relief is explicitly conditional and prospective. Without a firm-level model it cannot be a factual error. Requests for an all-inclusive €50 goal, stable funding and public financing of transformation costs are preferences. The 18 August authored date is preserved without a delivery inference.

Adequacy of consultation, need for an overall plan, insufficient recognition of regional actors and requests for pilots, energy sharing or fair conditions are policy judgments. Forecasts of acceptance, resilience, value creation and profitability are excluded. Concrete financing and physical mechanisms are inventoried. Footer population and budget boilerplate is low priority.
